findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
findings.body: The code destructures `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` into `mainHostDestinationCalendar` and then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array (handleNewBooking explicitly sets it to null when neither the event type nor organizer has one), this throws a TypeError during EventManager.create, breaking booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Google update/delete no longer fall back to the destination calendar
findings.body: In updateEvent and the analogous deleteEvent code, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` inside the branch where externalCalendarId is already falsy, so the find can never match and returns undefined. Previously this returned destinationCalendar.externalId. Updates therefore call Google with an undefined calendarId and deletes fall back to "primary", so reschedules/cancellations for events stored on a non-primary destination calendar fail or target the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services still create collective events only on the first host's calendar
findings.body: Office365 createEvent (like Lark at CalendarService.ts:128 and CalDAV at packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and ignores which credential the service instance was created for, even though EventManager now loops over every collective host's destination and invokes a separate credential's service. For the second and later hosts it therefore tries to write to the main host's externalId with another user's token, causing failures or events in the wrong calendar; it should select the destination whose credentialId matches the instance's credential (Google does this via the new credentialId argument).

findings.title: updateLocation now creates booking references without calendar/credential IDs
findings.body: updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult (CalendarManager.ts:313-322) never sets either field. Previously these came from evt.destinationCalendar. Edit-location therefore persists BookingReference rows with externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined, losing the link needed by later reschedule, update, and cancellation flows to target the correct external calendar.

findings.title: Collective team calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. The optional chain silently no-ops on null, so a collective event whose non-organizer hosts have destination calendars but whose organizer/event type does not will create no calendar events for those hosts, defeating the purpose of the change.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug persistence condition
findings.body: This file is unrelated to destinationCalendar, but the diff changes organization creation from setting `slug` when team billing is disabled (and `requestedSlug` in metadata when it is enabled) to setting both `slug` and `requestedSlug` only when team billing is enabled, and neither otherwise. Organizations created without team billing will now have no slug persisted, breaking org URL/domain handling that expects it.
